class.peasant.ANE: a farming family on temple land
class.landowner.ANE: a family of scribes and officials
class.slave.family.ANE: into a family of captives taken far from home
class.peasant.family.ANE: into a family of farmers who work temple or royal land
class.landowner.family.ANE: into the family of a scribe, priest or official with an estate
class.noble.family.ANE: into a noble family close to the court
prof.farmer.desc.ANE: Fields after the flood, barley and emmer, and a scribe who counts your harvest before you do.
prof.laborer.desc.ANE: You haul stone, dig canals and carry grain. The pay is bread and beer.
prof.artisan.desc.ANE: Copper, wood, leather, faience: a temple workshop or a shop of your own.
prof.weaver.desc.ANE: Linen in Egypt, wool in Mesopotamia. Fine cloth is worth its weight in silver.
prof.midwife.desc.ANE: Birthing bricks, spells and herbs. No family can do without you.
prof.merchant.desc.ANE: Agents of temples and palaces: shuty in Egypt, tamkarum in Mesopotamia. You trade grain for copper and copper for silver.
prof.sailor.desc.ANE: Barges on the river: grain, stone, passengers. Downstream is easy; upstream takes a sail and a pole.
prof.soldier.desc.ANE: Bow, spear and an oxhide shield. Campaigns to Canaan and Nubia — or north against neighbouring kings.
prof.scribe.desc.ANE: Barely one in a hundred can read and write. A scribe does not haul stone; he counts those who do.
prof.physician.desc.ANE: Swnw in Egypt, asû in Mesopotamia: ointments, bandages, spells and books of remedies.
prof.priest.desc.ANE: You serve in the temple in rotation with others: ritual washing, a shaved head, offerings to the god and a share of them.
prof.landholder.desc.ANE: Fields granted for service, workers, and an endless dispute with the treasury scribes.
prof.magistrate.desc.ANE: Mayor, governor or vizier: courts, taxes and reports to the king.
prof.matron.desc.ANE: "Mistress of the house" is the proud title of a woman in Egypt. Stores, servants, children and an account of everything.
prof.household_slave.desc.ANE: You were brought back from a campaign and given to a great house. You grind grain, carry water and serve at table.
prof.field_slave.desc.ANE: Work in the fields of a temple or the king, from flood to flood.
prof.officer.desc.ANE: Fifty archers or a squadron of chariots answer to you. Make a mistake and you answer to the king.
prof.shipowner.desc.ANE: Barges of your own on the river and a share in voyages to Byblos.
prof.official.desc.ANE: A scribe who has risen to hold a seal: granaries, courts, cattle counts.
prof.overseer.desc.ANE: A captive trusted with other captives and a granary.
prof.tomb_builder: Workman of the Place of Truth
prof.tomb_builder.as: a workman of the Place of Truth
prof.tomb_builder.desc: You cut and paint royal tombs in the Valley of the Kings, live in the closed village of Deir el-Medina and are paid in grain rations.
prof.embalmer.desc: Seventy days for every body: natron, resins, linen wrappings. A necessary trade, though people keep their distance.
prof.maryannu.desc: The maryannu are the elite of the army: a chariot of your own, a pair of horses, a bow and a driver. Costly, honoured and deadly.
prof.brewer.desc: Barley bread, water, dates — and a few days later thick beer that everyone drinks, from captive to priest.
prof.baru.desc: You read the will of the gods in the liver of a sacrificial lamb, in oil on water and in the stars. No king starts a war without you.
prof.potter.desc: Nile mud and a wheel: beer jars, bowls, bread moulds. There is always work, and the pay is always small.
prof.chantress.desc: You sing in the temple and shake the sistrum at festivals. An honoured title for women of good families.
lifestyle.food.varied.desc.ANE: Fish, dates, honey, meat on feast days
lifestyle.food.feasts.desc.ANE: Banquets with wine, musicians and dancers. Expensive
lifestyle.exercise.gymnasium.desc.ANE: Archery, wrestling, hunting in the marshes. Stronger and healthier
lifestyle.medicine.temple.desc.ANE: Amulets, prayers and spells from the priests of Sekhmet or Gula
lifestyle.medicine.physician.desc.ANE: A physician of your own watches over the family. Costly, but fewer die
lifestyle.baths.rarely.desc.ANE: A canal and a jar of water
lifestyle.baths.daily.desc.ANE: Every day: natron, oils and perfume. You need to live in town
focus.learn.desc.ANE: Learn to write on potsherds and tablets. The family will have to pay
focus.study.desc.ANE: A teacher, old texts, sums and the instructions of the sages. It costs money
focus.service.desc.ANE: Bow, spear and campaigns with the king's army
focus.religion.desc.ANE: Temples, offerings, amulets and festival processions
ev.c_h_family_doctor.text.ANE: A physician who has treated your neighbours makes an offer: for a regular fee he'll look after the whole family — give remedies, recite spells against illness and come at the first call.
ev.c_trade_high.text.ANE: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} has grown up. Friends advise: serving the gods brings honour, the scribal school brings respect and a post at the treasury, the family estate brings security. The choice is yours — but {npc} already has opinions.
ev.j_sol_recruiter.text.ANE: A royal herald has come to town: the army is gathering for a campaign, and those who come back are promised land and a share of the plunder. They say veterans of the last campaign now live in houses of their own.
ev.school_offer.text.ANE: Your family wonders whether to send you to scribal school. The teachers use the stick, but a scribe never hauls stone. It costs money, and they need your help at home now.
